# Captain Jim

- **Age:** 76 years old at the time of his death  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c15 P23](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0023)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c6 P9](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0009)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P25](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0025), [v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028), [v4 c40 P0](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0000)</sub>
- **Rank:** Captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P8](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0008)</sub>

- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper and former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c7 P29](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0029), [v4 c17 P0](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0000)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P8](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0008)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P8](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0008), [v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim was a tall, stooped, ungainly man of great strength and endurance, with a clean-shaven, deeply lined, bronzed face and a mane of iron-gray hair reaching to his shoulders. He possessed remarkably blue, deep-set eyes that sparkled or dreamed depending on his mood. Though plain in feature, his countenance was illuminated by a gentle, kindly spirit.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015)_

## Personality

Captain Jim possessed a gentle, humble, and chivalrous nature, maintaining an eternal youthfulness of heart despite a life filled with hardship and tragedy. He was a gifted, natural-born storyteller who delighted in sharing tales of his seafaring adventures with those he considered kindred spirits. Deeply compassionate toward all suffering creatures, he harbored a tender love for children and animals. He faced life's trials and the prospect of death with serene cheerfulness, humor, and a quiet, steadfast faith.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015), [v4 c9 P46](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0046), [v4 c9 P49](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0049), [v4 c9 P50](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0050), [v4 c15 P8](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0008), [v4 c15 P15](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0015), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018), [v4 c35 P36](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0036)_

## Goals

- To have his life-book written and published so his memories would not be forgotten  <sub>[v4 c17 P20](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0020), [v4 c25 P5](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0005)</sub>
- To preserve the memory of his lost love, Margaret  <sub>[v4 c15 P5](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0005)</sub>

## History

Captain Jim spent his youth in Four Winds, where he befriended John Selwyn, the local schoolmaster, and witnessed the arrival of Selwyn's bride to their new home on the harbor shore. In his teens he ran away to sea, spending decades sailing the globe and experiencing shipwreck, mutiny, marooning, and battles. In his youth he loved a girl named Margaret, but she tragically drowned in a summer squall, an event that left an enduring mark on his life. Years later, while in Havana, he discovered an amnesiac sailor whom he believed to be Dick Moore, bringing him back to his wife Leslie. Retiring from the sea, Captain Jim became the keeper of the Four Winds Light, living a quiet life accompanied by his cat, the First Mate. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved into the old Selwyn house, he instantly recognized them as 'kindred spirits' belonging to 'the race that knows Joseph' and became a cherished friend. Later, when John Selwyn's grandson, Owen Ford, visited Four Winds, Captain Jim entrusted him with his manuscript 'life-book.' Owen adapted these real-life adventures into a highly successful novel. Shortly after receiving and reading the published book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, his hands resting on his life-book.

## Background by volume

- Born at Four Winds, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- Ran away to sea as a boy and spent most of his life sailing the world  <sub>[v4 c7 P29](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0029), [v4 c9 P40](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0040)</sub>
- Was deeply in love with a girl named Margaret who drowned fifty years prior  <sub>[v4 c20 P12](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0012), [v4 c20 P17](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0017)</sub>
- Rescued Dick Moore (later identified as George Moore) in Havana and brought him home  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c13 P13](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0013), [v4 c32 P13](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0013)</sub>
- Kept a detailed 'life-book' journal recording his adventures and travels  <sub>[v4 c9 P36](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0036), [v4 c17 P19](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0019)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m ninety-nine hundredths a sailor, and only one-hundredth a landlubber.  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>

> You’re young and I’m old, but our souls are about the same age, I reckon. We both belong to the race that knows Joseph, as Cornelia Bryant would say.  <sub>[v4 c7 P55](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0055)</sub>

> The race that knows Joseph is the salt of the airth, I reckon.  <sub>[v4 c7 P59](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0059)</sub>

> If it wasn’t for our dreams they might as well bury us. How’d we stand living if it wasn’t for our dream of immortality?  <sub>[v4 c20 P9](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0009)</sub>

> There’s no two sides to that, in my opinion. It’s what’s right that we’ve got to do, no matter what it costs us.  <sub>[v4 c30 P7](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0007)</sub>
